caption:
Bitcoin miner Riot Platforms has leased its entire Corsicana, Texas campus to Anthropic.
The 15-year deal covers 910 megawatts and is worth about $28 billion. Riot's quarterly filing names Anthropic as the tenant.
The first 400 megawatts are due in September 2027.

paragraphs.text: Bitcoin miner Riot Platforms announced on November 4, 2026 that it had signed the largest lease in its history: a 15-year agreement covering its entire Corsicana campus in Texas. The company valued the deal at about $28 billion of contracted revenue over the initial term.

Riot's earnings release described the tenant only as a leading frontier AI lab. Its quarterly report filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on the same day identifies the company: the lease was signed with Anthropic PBC, the maker of Claude.

The agreement covers 910 megawatts of critical IT capacity on a single 332-acre parcel. It is a triple net powered land lease, meaning Riot provides the land, the power connection and the electrical infrastructure, while the tenant owns and operates the computing equipment and pays the operating expenses. Two optional five-year extensions could raise the total value to about $54 billion, according to Riot.

Riot said average annual rent, including escalators, will be about $1.8 billion over the initial term. It estimated total capital costs at about $6 million per IT megawatt, or $5.5 billion. Riot pays about $2 million per megawatt for site work and electrical systems, and the remaining $4 million per megawatt is reimbursed to the tenant in phases once each phase is delivered and paying rent.

Capacity will be handed over in three phases: 400 megawatts in September 2027, 200 megawatts in January 2028 and 310 megawatts in July 2028. Rent on each phase starts no later than 60 days after delivery. Riot expects to fund the reimbursements with non-recourse project debt, and if that financing is not available on comparable terms, the tenant funds them and recovers the cost through rent credits. Cointelegraph reported that the financing has not yet been secured.

The campus was built for bitcoin mining, and Cointelegraph reported that mining at Corsicana could wind down starting in summer 2027. Riot chief executive Jason Les said in the release that the company does not currently expect to issue new shares to pay for its announced projects. Riot shares rose more than 13% on November 4, according to Cointelegraph.

Corsicana is not Riot's first lease with the same frontier AI lab. In August, Riot disclosed a 191 megawatt, 20-year lease at its Rockdale site in Texas, and Bloomberg reported at the time that Anthropic was the tenant, according to The Decoder. That deal was valued at $9.1 billion before extensions. The new 10-Q uses the same defined term for both tenants but names Anthropic only in connection with Corsicana.
Riot now reports 1,151 megawatts of critical IT capacity under lease across its sites, representing about $38 billion of long-term contracted data center revenue, including an agreement with AMD.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the deal shows how much Anthropic is willing to commit for guaranteed power years in advance. Former bitcoin mining sites come with what AI companies need most, large grid connections and land that is already zoned for heavy electrical use, and Riot is pricing that advantage into long-term contracts rather than relying on the price of bitcoin.
The first test is September 2027, when the initial 400 megawatts are due, and whether Riot closes the project debt it needs before then.
